title: Residue reduction is conservative on locally complete objects
statement: Let X be a scheme, A a commutative Noetherian ring, J an ideal and U an object of the coefficient-sized pro-etale site. Use completed coefficients and reductions of [def-sfb-adic-residue-lift-comparisons]. Let T,M in D(B_X|U) both be locally complete for ker(q_0). If f:T -> M has invertible derived residue reduction R_0(f), then f is invertible. No constructibility, boundedness, finite Tor amplitude, or perfectness of the quotients over A is assumed.

source.place: Tag 09C6, final complete-cone argument; Algebraization Tags 099M and 099F for quotient completion and derived Nakayama.

proof.text: Complete f:T -> M to a distinguished triangle with cone Q. The Koszul-completion unit is a natural map of exact functors, so its isomorphism criterion and two-out-of-three show Q is locally complete. The exact reduction functor takes this triangle to one whose first map is invertible, so its residue cone Q_0 is zero. Choose a flat-term K-flat model of Res Q. Tensor the exact constant coefficient sequence 0 -> J^n/J^(n+1) -> A/J^(n+1) -> A/J^n -> 0 with it. Exact constant realization and flatness give the coefficient triangle. Reassociation identifies the first term with Q_0 tensor^L_(A/J) (J^n/J^(n+1)), hence with zero. Starting at exponent one, induction gives zero for every quotient reduction Q_n. Completeness identifies Q with their derived inverse limit, which is zero. The distinguished cone triangle then makes f invertible. All constructions and equalities take place on the specified slice, preserving the original quotient action; no finiteness as sets or perfectness of A/J^n over A is used.
